items.title: Daniel Lurie Wins San Francisco Mayoral Race
items.summary: Daniel Lurie, a nonprofit founder and political outsider, won the San Francisco mayoral race after defeating incumbent London Breed.
items.excerpt: Daniel Lurie won San Francisco's mayoral race with 56% of votes after ranked-choice tallies, defeating incumbent Mayor London Breed who had 43%. Lurie ran as the only major candidate without city hall experience, positioning himself as an outsider who could address corruption and bring change to San Francisco government.

items.title: Daniel Lurie inaugurated as San Francisco's 46th mayor, followed by celebrations; outlines vision for city
items.summary: Daniel Lurie was sworn in as San Francisco's 46th mayor, vowing to restore trust in government and address homelessness and the fentanyl crisis.
items.excerpt: Daniel Lurie was inaugurated as San Francisco's 46th mayor on January 8, 2026, at Civic Center Plaza. He promised to focus on tackling homelessness, the fentanyl crisis, improving city services, and revitalizing downtown, while acknowledging that change doesn't happen overnight.

items.title: Mayor Lurie on San Francisco: 'We Are On Our Way Back. But We Still Have Work To Do.'
items.summary: Mayor Lurie delivered his first State of the City address, emphasizing progress on crime while acknowledging affordability remains a key challenge.
items.excerpt: In his first State of the City Address at Rossi Park on January 15, 2026, Mayor Lurie boasted about crime progress but stressed that affordability remains a major problem for working families. He emphasized the need for MUNI and BART funding, accessible City College programs, and streamlined small business permitting.

items.title: Daniel Lurie was the public safety mayor. Now he's trying to be the affordability guy
items.summary: Mayor Lurie shifted his messaging focus from public safety to affordability in his first State of the City speech.
items.excerpt: In his first State of the City speech, Mayor Lurie pivoted from his previous emphasis on crime and public safety to focus on affordability issues affecting working families. He came out against California's proposed 5% wealth tax on billionaires, expressing concerns it would drive people out of the state.

items.title: Mayor Lurie Presents Balanced, Responsible Budget to Advance San Francisco's Recovery
items.summary: Mayor Lurie presented a $15.9 billion budget for fiscal years 2025-2027, closing an $800 million deficit while prioritizing public safety and core services.
items.excerpt: Mayor Lurie presented his first budget of $15.9 billion for fiscal years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027, closing a historic $800 million deficit through structural changes. The budget prioritizes public safety, clean streets, behavioral health crisis response, economic revitalization, and supports small businesses while creating a new city agency to strengthen arts and culture.

items.title: Lurie reflects on first year in office as 2025 draws to a close
items.summary: Mayor Lurie reflected on his first year, citing 30% citywide crime reduction and progress on street conditions.
items.excerpt: As 2025 ended, Mayor Lurie touted significant progress including a 30% citywide crime reduction, 44% decrease in encampments, 40% increase in shelter placements, and 500 new treatment beds. He acknowledged making mistakes but expressed optimism for 2026 with major events like the Super Bowl and World Cup coming to the Bay Area.

items.title: S.F. mayor, board president propose 3 ballot measures to boost executive power
items.summary: Mayor Lurie and Board President Mandelman proposed three November ballot measures to expand executive power and reform San Francisco's charter.
items.excerpt: Mayor Lurie and Board of Supervisors President Rafael Mandelman proposed three ballot measures to reform San Francisco's charter, expanding the power of the mayor and city administrator while reducing power from oversight commissions and the Board of Supervisors. Critics, including labor leaders, expressed concern about consolidation of power and reduced public participation.

items.title: Mayor Lurie, Sup. Mandelman Introduce Ballot Measures Aimed at Reforming City Charter
items.summary: Three proposed charter reform measures would reshape how City Hall works, including tightening ballot initiative requirements and expanding mayoral authority.
items.excerpt: The three proposed ballot measures would overhaul contracting rules, tighten the initiative process by increasing signature requirements from 2% to 8% of registered voters, and expand the mayor's authority to hire and fire department heads directly. Each measure needs roughly 51,000 voter signatures to qualify for the November 2026 ballot.

items.title: San Francisco layoffs begin as Mayor Lurie looks to close deficit
items.summary: Mayor Lurie ordered 127 layoffs across 18 departments as part of efforts to address a massive budget shortfall projected to reach $1 billion.
items.excerpt: Mayor Lurie announced the first wave of 127 layoffs across 18 departments in April 2026, with expectations of about 500 total cuts including vacant positions. The mayor cited new federal and state funding cuts and warned that the budget gap could reach $1 billion in coming years without action.

items.title: Mayor Lurie moves S.F. homeless street-outreach teams to health department
items.summary: Mayor Lurie moved street-outreach teams from Emergency Management to the Department of Public Health, emphasizing health-focused approaches to homelessness and addiction.
items.excerpt: Mayor Lurie transferred San Francisco's street-outreach teams from the Department of Emergency Management to the Department of Public Health, signaling that addressing health factors is key to fighting drug use and homelessness. Around 20 city workers and 100 contracted workers now report to the health department under this restructuring.

items.title: Lurie Appoints SF's First Arts Director, Forges Arts Partnerships In Shanghai
items.summary: Mayor Lurie appointed Matthew Goudeau as San Francisco's first executive director of arts and culture and signed partnerships with Shanghai arts organizations.
items.excerpt: Mayor Lurie appointed Matthew Goudeau as the city's first executive director of arts and culture following a search with over 250 applicants. The appointment followed Lurie's trip to Asia where he signed eight memoranda of understanding in Shanghai to strengthen partnerships between San Francisco and Chinese arts organizations.

items.title: Mayor touts low homeless count, but critics say methodology was flawed
items.summary: Mayor Lurie announced a 22% decline in unsheltered residents to a 15-year low, but the count used new methodology criticized by homeless advocates.
items.excerpt: The January 2026 Point in Time Count found 3,400 unsheltered residents, a 22% decline from 2024 and the lowest since 2011. However, the count used a different methodology than previous years, including different hours and requiring verbal interactions, leading homeless advocates to question the validity of comparisons with prior years.
